description: Not a lever: a measurement. The opt-in smoke tests agent_turns and agent_turns_long (c2_serving_smoke.py) reproduce what production agent traffic does to the card and the concurrent8_steady / code_32k / code_128k shapes do not: six concurrent coding sessions on 64k / 128k / 200k real-code contexts, each appending a deterministic 150-400 token tool-result message after the assistant's previous answer verbatim, generating 200-600 tokens and waiting a 1-8 s tool gap, so a returning turn appends a few hundred tokens, re-prefills a few thousand old ones behind the resume checkpoint and pays an engine rebind. It reports per turn the prompt, cached and re-prefilled tokens, TTFT and decode tok/s; per session and in total the committed tok/s, TTFT by context and a per-live-users table; and, from the container log (every request carries an X-Request-Id tag that names it in the engine's lines), the prefill and decode shares of the wall time and the server-side per-live table. scripts/ci/agent_turns.py holds the plan, the numbers, the log reader and the judge (`python3 scripts/ci/agent_turns.py plan|report`); c2_smoke_check.agent_turns_problems judges it: errors and timeouts fail, otherwise it is a measurement, and on a prefix-reuse profile a salted run must reuse on 90% of its returning turns (an unsalted one fails unless SMOKE_AGENT_SALT=none asks for the control). Nothing on a device and nothing in a profile.
notes: Opt-in: nothing runs unless C2_SMOKE_TESTS names agent_turns (about 13 minutes at the defaults, 6 sessions x 12 returning turns) or agent_turns_long (6 x 30, about 24 minutes). A four-card smoke job on an eight-seat profile must also name concurrent8_steady (or C2_SMOKE_PARTIAL). No image file: the smoke client and the check run from the checkout on the host (agent_turns.py is not served, so no overlay line). Shared files this branch DID edit: c2_serving_smoke.py (the two tests; stream() takes a headers argument and reports cached_tokens when the usage carries prompt_tokens_details), c2_smoke_check.py (agent_turns_problems, called from check) and .github/workflows/qwen-c2-serving.yml (the four-card smoke step writes a throwaway salt key and mounts it into the container when, and only when, the job names one of the two tests, so the sessions' cache_salt verifies; without it a prefix-reuse profile runs unsalted and reuse is inert).
